title: Longest common subsequence

cases.name: one is a subsequence of the other
two strings of 1,500 letters
cases.stdin_py: ''.join('ACGT'[(i * i + 3 * i) % 4] for i in range(1500)) + '\n' + ''.join('ACGT'[(i * 7 + i // 3) % 4] for i in range(1500)) + '\n'

hints: dp[i][j] is the answer for the first i characters of a and the first j characters of b. Row 0 and column 0 are all zero.
If a[i-1] == b[j-1], then dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1. Otherwise it is the larger of dp[i-1][j] and dp[i][j-1].
The answer is in the last cell, dp[len(a)][len(b)].
